answer: An atlas of attestations is a graph in which trust propagates from trusted seeds through bounded random walks, with voting weight derived from the resulting reachability. A Sybil garden may contain many mutually attesting identities, but if its external cut is sparse, its conductance is low: few walk paths cross from honest nodes into the cluster. Under fixed seeds and walk length, this limits reachable Sybil mass, bounding aggregate voting weight; a falcon of colluding accounts cannot amplify influence merely by multiplying identities.
